notes: CLOSING AN INSTRUMENT FROM EDIT INPUTS NOW ACTUALLY WORKS, SHOWS ITS STATE, AND CAN BE UNDONE. THE BUG: the timeline save had two branches. The Instruments page wrote to state, saved, re-rendered and raised the matching redemption. The Edit-inputs branch did one thing — 'ctx.row._events = sorted' onto a DOM node — and relied on the user triggering a step save afterwards. Nothing persisted, nothing re-rendered, no redemption was offered. The button opened the modal and the modal accepted input, which is why it looked functional while doing nothing. FIXED: the Edit-inputs branch now resolves the row back to its state object by id, writes the events, saves immediately, refreshes the row, and applies the same redemption rule as the Instruments page — a close dated at or before this month raises the full redemption as a Journal entry, a future close stays projection-only. CLOSED STATE IS NOW VISIBLE AND REVERSIBLE: a closed row is dimmed with a dashed border and carries a chip reading 'Closed from YYYY-MM — no longer counted after this' with a Reopen control beside it. Closing is easy to do by accident and was previously invisible on this page, the only hint being a tinted badge on the timeline button. Reopen removes the close event, persists, and restores the row. VERIFIED END TO END, BOTH INSTRUMENT TYPES. EMI: event persisted to state; row dimmed with chip; active in Dec 2026 and inactive in Feb 2027; engine charges Rs 52,000 in December and Rs 0 in February; readEMIs preserves the event; Reopen clears it and the February charge returns to Rs 52,000. Investment: event persisted; row dimmed with chip; balance Rs 6,96,499 in Feb 2027 falling to Rs 0 by April; contributions stop; readInvestments preserves the event; Reopen restores the April balance to Rs 7,63,499. ALSO: the duplicate timeline button introduced in the previous release has been removed — both row types had always had one, created in different ways. STILL UNVERIFIED, STATED PLAINLY: hiding a closed instrument's ROW from the projection sheet works for EMIs but could not be confirmed for investments. A closed investment correctly reports a zero balance, so the row should drop out, but in testing it stayed visible and the cause was not found. This is cosmetic — the instrument is genuinely closed and contributes nothing — but it is worth checking and reporting rather than assuming. Regression confirms the Projection-to-Dashboard and Decisions-to-chain gaps both remain zero. No page errors.
